Yes, that is correct. In Swiss referendums, each of the 26 cantons is allocated one vote, regardless of its population size. For a proposal to be accepted, it must meet two thresholds simultaneously: 

1. A simple majority of all eligible voters nationwide must vote in favor of the proposal.
2. A simple majority of the cantons (i.e., at least 13 out of 26 cantons) must also vote in favor of the proposal.

This dual-majority requirement ensures that both the popular will and the will of the cantons are considered, reflecting the federal structure of Switzerland.
